comparison: Perfect agreement on DDX6 KO cell line generation and validation (C43, C44). Both accept the knockout methodology and validation as sound without raising concerns.

Both address the speculative claim about CAG repeat implications (C115). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct evidence for proteostasis disruption, while peer reviewers accept the speculation as appropriately framed without challenge.

Strong agreement on core DDX6 role in mRNA decay (C40-C47). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by Figure 1 data with quantified measurements. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm findings as 'convincing' and 'clearly demonstrated' with evolutionary conservation.

Agreement on sequence characteristics of DDX6 targets (C87-C92). Both accept the decreased GC content and low codon optimality findings. OpenEval notes statistical significance; peer reviewers accept characterization without specific concerns.

Strong agreement on reporter validation experiments (C103-C108). OpenEval finds data well-supported with appropriate controls; peer reviewers explicitly state validation 'confirmed' DDX6-dependent degradation and accept reporter experiments as sound.

Agreement on transcriptome-wide profiling results (C79-C86). OpenEval finds RNA-seq and ribosome profiling data well-supported with proper statistical thresholds. Peer reviewers accept the 260 mRNA identification, though suggest analysis could be more in-depth (improvement suggestion, not challenge).

Agreement on mechanistic distinction (C53-C54). Both accept that DDX6 does not directly modulate CCR4-NOT activity but acts through alternative mechanism. OpenEval notes mechanism remains unclear; peer reviewers accept finding without challenge.

Agreement on qPCR validation and target identification (C99-C102). OpenEval notes reasonable validation rate (67%) and appropriate transparency about discrepancies. Peer reviewers accept validation experiments showing 'certainty' for transcripts with repetitive sequences.

Strong agreement on mutant analysis demonstrating multiple DDX6 functions required (C68-C73). OpenEval finds systematic testing convincing with proper expression controls. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'determined that all known functional domains...are required' and accept comprehensive analysis.

Agreement on CCR4-NOT pathway involvement (C50-C51). OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 1D-E data. Peer reviewers accept mechanistic finding as 'sound, with proper controls' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C109-C112, C116). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by collective experimental findings. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse with 'convincing' evidence, 'valuable findings,' and 'clearly demonstrated' results.

Agreement on DDX6-ribosome interaction and domain mapping (C56, C58-C60). OpenEval finds pulldown and co-IP data provide converging evidence, noting RNase I caveat. Peer reviewers highlight this as novel contribution, specifically noting FDF motif mediation without raising concerns.

Agreement on background/contextual claims (C1-C25 overlap). OpenEval categorizes as well-established literature-based context with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept background without challenge, explicitly affirming evolutionary conservation context.

Agreement on mutant analysis of interaction surfaces (C63-C65, C67). OpenEval finds experimental design appropriate with proper folding controls. Peer reviewers accept domain mapping and FDF motif findings as part of novel contribution without concerns.

Agreement on mRNA decay pathway background (C26-C39). OpenEval categorizes as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept background context, noting work 'confirms' conservation with yeast homolog Dhh1.

Agreement on translational efficiency findings (C93-C94). OpenEval notes DDX6-regulated mRNAs don't have lower baseline TE, suggesting DDX6 prevents more efficient translation. Peer reviewers accept as part of ribosome profiling analysis consistent with overall model.

Agreement on identification of specific targets with stalling sequences (C95-C96, C99-C102 overlap). OpenEval notes manual screening identified AR with CAG repeats, cites preprint caveat. Peer reviewers accept identification of 35 transcripts and validation 'with certainty' for repetitive sequences.

Agreement on evolutionary conservation (C57). OpenEval finds conservation claim appropriately drawn from yeast comparison. Peer reviewers explicitly emphasize 'evolutionary conservation of this process across Eukaryotes' as central positive assessment.

Agreement on overarching conclusion (C116). OpenEval finds dual role in translation and stability supported by collective findings. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse summary conclusions as 'convincing' with 'major insight' into DDX6 role.

Agreement on folding control for Mut2 (C66). OpenEval notes control addresses folding concerns for interpreting ribosome binding loss. Peer reviewers accept control as part of sound experimental design without challenge.

Agreement on ribosome profiling methodology background (C74-C78). OpenEval categorizes as established methodology with foundational citations. Peer reviewers accept methodological context without concerns.
